title: They always preach the giant.
paragraphs: They shout about Goliath falling, about faith conquering fear, about the underdog winning.
But they rush past a detail that refuses to be random.
“And he took his staff in his hand and chose for himself five smooth stones from the brook…” — 1 Samuel 17:40
And that number sits there quietly, like something God hid in plain sight.
You don’t walk into a valley with a lion-killing past, a bear-killing testimony, and suddenly become careless with preparation.
A giant mocking the living God.
And in the middle of it all—David bends down… calmly.
Silence inside him while chaos screams around him.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
David had already won before the stone ever left his sling.
Because his confidence wasn’t in the stone.
It was in the God who trained his hands in secret.
“When a lion or a bear came… I struck it and delivered the lamb…” — 1 Samuel 17:34-35
He didn’t discover courage in the spotlight.
He developed it where nobody was watching.
And that’s where you start to feel the weight of this.
Because you’ve been asking God for public victories…
You wanted the Goliath moment without the wilderness process.
But David’s five stones weren’t panic.
Some believe it was wisdom—preparation in case the first didn’t land.
Some see deeper—Goliath had brothers (2 Samuel 21:15-22), and David wasn’t just thinking about one battle.
Others see something even more piercing…
Because victory was never about David’s aim.
Because you’ve been trying to fight your battles with one stone.
One last attempt before giving up.
But David stepped in fully prepared—not because he doubted God…
…but because he trusted Him enough to act wisely.
Faith moves with conviction and clarity.
“Some trust in chariots, and some in horses; but we will remember the name of the Lord our God.” — Psalm 20:7
But because a shepherd boy understood something kings had forgotten.
God fights for those who stand in His name.
And this is where it stops being about David…
Because you’ve been facing giants too.
Not nine feet tall—but just as loud.
Sin that keeps calling you back.
You tell yourself it’s not that serious.
And here’s the tension you’ve been avoiding—
You cannot defeat spiritual giants while holding onto the very sin that empowers them.
David didn’t walk into that valley divided.
“But the Lord said… man looks at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.” — 1 Samuel 16:7
That’s where the real battle is.
And here’s the truth that breaks everything open—
You don’t just need better strategy.
Because your greatest enemy isn’t in front of you.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
And no number of stones can fix that.
“But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
This is the moment everything changes.
Jesus won your soul—if you’ll surrender it.
And now you’re standing in your own valley.
That quiet voice saying, “This is about you.”
You can keep pretending your “five stones” are enough…
Or you can admit what David already knew—
So here’s the line you’re standing on—
One version of you keeps playing games with sin, delaying surrender, hoping things somehow change.
The other finally drops the pride… and turns to Christ fully.
Out loud if you have to.
Follow this path if you’re done with surface-level faith and ready for truth that actually transforms.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—real growth, real correction, real discipleship that doesn’t compromise—
It’s about the God who never misses.
